pov.first_person: First person past tense (I, me, my). A survivor telling you what happened.
pov.second_person: Second person present tense (you, your), as if it is happening to the viewer.
pov.third_person: Close third person past tense following one named character.
pov.witness: First person, but the narrator is a witness describing what happened to someone else they knew.

formats.real_time: Real-time single-location incident where events unfold minute by minute.
formats.evidence: Recovered evidence narrative anchored on logs, messages, or recordings.
formats.confession: Confession where the narrator admits what they did after the event.
formats.rule: Rule-based setup where breaking one specific rule triggers escalating danger.
formats.countdown: Countdown tied to a specific time limit before the reveal.
formats.false_safe: False-safe scenario where an apparent rescue becomes the final threat.

endings.was_the_threat: The narrator or protagonist turns out to have been the threat all along.
endings.too_late: The protagonist solves it, but the answer arrives too late and costs them everything.
endings.survives_changed: The protagonist escapes, but a final concrete detail shows what it permanently took from them.
endings.trusted_betrayer: The person the protagonist trusted most is revealed as the cause, with proof.
endings.already_dead: A planted detail proves someone in the story has been dead the whole time.
endings.threat_defeated_at_cost: The threat is actually stopped, and we learn the terrible price that was paid.
endings.true_purpose: The strange events are revealed to have had a specific, horrifying purpose, now fulfilled.
